title.en: Motion: hands-on activities from the textbook

text.en: Motion becomes clear when you throw a ball, plot a graph and spin a marble. Chapter 4 turns these into activities.

Activity 4.1 throws a ball straight up from O to a highest point B and back to O. Distance is the total path, so it adds the up and down paths, while displacement is the straight change of position and is zero when the ball returns to O.
Activity 4.2 finds average acceleration. Look up the time a car takes to go from 0 to 100 km per hour and divide the change in speed by that time.
For example 100 km per hour is about 27.8 m per second, so a car taking 10 seconds has an acceleration of about 2.8 m per second squared.
Activity 4.3 teaches graph plotting. Draw the X-axis and Y-axis on graph paper, decide which quantity goes on which axis, mark points from the table and join them.
Activity 4.4 shows the slope of a position-time graph. A triangle drawn on a straight section gives change in position divided by change in time, which is the velocity.
A car moving at a steady 72 km per hour, which is 20 m per second, has a horizontal velocity-time graph. A car starting from rest whose velocity increases steadily gives a slanted straight line.
Activity 4.5 sends a marble round the inside of a ring. If you lift the ring, the marble leaves the circle and moves in a straight line.
This shows that the direction of motion keeps changing in circular motion, so it is accelerated motion even at steady speed.

problem.en: A car goes from 0 to 27.8 m per second in 10 seconds. Find its average acceleration.

text.en: Change in speed = 27.8 - 0 = 27.8 m per second.

prompt.en: Explain the difference between distance and displacement with the ball-throwing activity.

requiredIdeas.en: Distance is the total path travelled
Displacement is zero at the start point

points.en: Distance is path length; displacement is the straight change of position.
Acceleration = change in speed divided by time.
Slope of a position-time graph gives velocity.
A marble leaving a ring moves in a straight line.
